Subject: Blister packs for Margaret Kerrigan — welcome to Erindale Park Pharmacy

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for writing to us, and welcome to Erindale Park Pharmacy. I am Rania Haddad, the community pharmacist here, and I will be looking after Margaret's medications myself. I am glad to hear she is coming home Thursday, and I will do what I can so that her blister packs are in place before she is settled back in.

Blister packs and cost
Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs arranged for seven days at four times a day. There is no charge for the packaging itself. Margaret will simply pay her normal dispensing fee, and at 81 most of that is covered by the Ontario Drug Benefit.

Delivery or pickup
We deliver free of charge within 8 km of the pharmacy, and her building on Mississauga Valley Blvd is comfortably within that area. Our regular delivery days are Tuesdays and Fridays, 2 to 6 pm. Since she is arriving home on Thursday, we can either make a one-off delivery on Saturday before 1 pm, or you are very welcome to collect the packs from the store. Once we are established, we can also place her on our regular Tuesday delivery.

Moving her prescriptions to us
There is no form for Margaret to sign for this. I only need the name and address of her current pharmacy on Dundas and her OHIP health card number, and I will call them and have the records transferred over.

Going over the new medication list
I would be glad to review her new medications with you, either in person at the store or by phone in the evening, and to make sure she is comfortable with the new routine. Before we are able to discuss Margaret's prescriptions with anyone else, we do need her signed permission, so we use a short Family Communication Consent form. It is entirely for Margaret's benefit and protects her privacy: she remains the patient, and her medication information stays confidential with us. She can sign it here at the store, or I will send it with the driver for her to sign at home.

Two requests, please
First, to have her first packs ready on Saturday, could you ask the discharge team to fax or e-prescribe her prescriptions to us early on Thursday and let us know if any part of the list will follow later? Once we have all of them, our technician needs about 48 hours to build the packs properly.

Second, as the first packs will not be ready on Thursday itself, please speak with the discharge team about an interim supply — enough medication to cover her at home until Saturday — and help her with every dose until we deliver or you collect. It is a short bridge, and it keeps her from missing anything while she is still recovering.

A medication review at home
Once she is home, I would also like to offer a MedsCheck: a free 20-minute review in which I come to her home and check every medication against her list, the bottles and the packaging. I can come Monday or Tuesday evening, after 6 pm, whichever suits her better. There is no charge for this service.

If anything is easier to discuss by phone than in writing, you can reach me directly on 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm.

I look forward to looking after Margaret.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad
Community Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
Direct: 905-555-0148 ext. 2
